When I try and read in a SNP dataset using gl.read.csv, it fails within the function at the line:

gl <- gl.recalc.metrics(gl)

With this error:

Warning: Locus metafile not provided, locus metrics will be

Input data should be a csv file with individuals as rows, loci as columns

Numeric data detected, assume genotypes are 0 = homozygous reference, 1 = heterozygous, 2 = homozygous alternate
Starting gl.recalc.metrics
  Processing  Presence/Absence (SilicoDArT) data
Starting utils.recalc.avgpic
  Processing  Presence/Absence (SilicoDArT) data, locus metric PIC
Error in if (x@other$loc.metrics.flags$monomorphs == FALSE) { :
  argument is of length zero
In addition: Warning messages:

2: In apply(data, 2, as.numeric) : NAs introduced by coercion

For some reason, even though the data is coded 0/1/2, it thinks it is silicodart instead of SNPs. Any thoughts on why this could be happening?

Thanks,

Renee

messages.subject: dartr 1.9.9.1 on CRAN has a bug with lat lon
messages.subject_clean: dartr 1.9.9.1 on CRAN has a bug with lat lon
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

we just noticed (thanks Renee) that the latest CRAN version has a "severe" bug, if you want to work with lat lon coordinates [good old latlong / latlon confusion].

We bascially tried to rectify the old legacy spelling but introduced an error (read more details below).  In a nut-shell. If you want to have a working gl.map.interactive or also gl2shp and a new gl.ibd then you need to do the following

install the CRAN version
install.packages("dartR")  #CRAN version 1.9.9.1 if you do not have it already

library(dartR)
packageVersion("dartR") #should be 1.9.9.1

#update to the dev version on Github
gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")
packageVersion("dartR") #should be 1.9.9.7 now
which installs the current dev version on your system.

This has unfortunately the other repercussion that not all new functions are fully tested and we did quite a few changes. We wanted to wait for this until we have consolidated, but the latlong bug on CRAN is severe enough to risk it. So if you have problems with gl.map.interactive you might try to install the dev version.

If this does not work for you you can go back to 1.9.9.1 using
install.packages("dartR")

For a more detailed explanation:
The new lat lon naming is now more consistent. The coordinates are stored now under

gl@other$latlon [not long anymore].

The good news is that the system is backward compatible so if you have older genlight object that sill use @other$latlong the new function work or you can use

glnew <- gl.compliance.check(gl)
to rename the coordinates to the correct latlon slot.

new gl.ibd (isolation by distance analysis).
This function has now received a new overhaul. It allows to calculate several pairwise distances (individuals based and population based) and also any transformation of the genetic and geographic distances. As a new feature you can now also plot an pairwise individual distances (so 1-proportionofshared alleles) but color the dots by the population identity of individuals. A example for bandicoots.gl <http://bandicoots.gl> is obtained via:

gl.ibd(bandicoots.gl <http://bandicoots.gl>, distance="propShared", pairscol="pop", Dgeo_trans="log(Dgeo)")

It also projects now coordinates from lat lon s, runs the mantel test and returns the coefficients, or the fitted line (might be interesting in some cases).

Sorry for the inconvenience,

Cheers, Bernd

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

potentially a pretty basic question, but I've just been pottering around with private alleles and used gl.report.pa <http://gl.report.pa> to get some estimates. I kind of get the idea to compare populations pairwise, but I always thought that, per definition, Private alleles are alleles that are found only in a single population among a broader collection of populations. This would deliver one value per population, when comparing e.g. 5 populations. Is there any way to manipulate the code to compare one pop against the other 4 and repeat that for each pop (I hope that makes sense)?
Further, looking at the output, I get huge values for 'priv1', 'priv2' and therefore 'totalpriv'. I do compare populations on a somewhat larger scale but not massive. E.g. I used ~2000 loci on ~10 indiviuals per pop. Comparing pop1 and pop 2, which are geographically very close to each other, priv1 = 325 and priv2=323m with totalpriv = 648, and mdf of 0.165. Could you help me to put this result in words? I'm not sure I interpret the colums correctly. Does this mean pop1 compared to pop2 has 325 private alleles?

Thanks alread in advance,

best wishes,
Katrin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Katrin,

If you have all five populations in the data, you should get a whole matrix of comparisons out. If you want to compare p1 to the other four populations as a whole, then you would need to just reassign those four populations to a single p2 population and do it 5 times.

Your example means there are 325 private alleles in p1 that are not in p2, and 323 private alleles in p2 that are not in p1, for a total number of 648 private alleles between the two populations.

Hope that helps.

Renee

@Katrin

Renee explained it nicely.

pas <- list

The shortcut could be copy your genlight object with the 5 pops and recode 1 against 2-5, e.g. via

for (i in 1:5)

{

gl2  <- gl

pop(gl2) <- factor(ifelse(pop(gl2)==popNames(gl)[i],popNames(gl)[i], “rest”))

print(pas[[i]] <- gl.report.pa <http://gl.report.pa>(gl2))

flush.console() #just so you see the output in a loop.

}

pas is then a list with all the five comparisons…

I have not tested this, so not sure if it works.

Cheers, Bernd

pas<- list()
for (i in 1:6)

{

  gl2  <- gl

  pop(gl2) <- factor(ifelse(pop(gl2)==popNames(gl)[i],popNames(gl)[i], 'zest'))

  print(prival[[i]] <- gl.report.pa <http://gl.report.pa>(gl2))

  flush.console() #just so you see the output in a loop.

}
pas

messages.body_plain:
dartR does not currently have options for changing the colour, size or shape of points in the PCoA. I have raised this as an issue on gitHub, and this capability should be added to dartR when version 2 is released. In the meantime, you can try the workaround suggested by Luis.

On Tuesday, June 29, 2021 at 10:37:08 AM UTC+10 luis.m...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi Dallas,
>
> Could you please try the code below.
>
> Please let us know whether it worked for you.
>
> Cheers,
> Luis
>
> library(plotly)
> gl <- testset.gl <http://testset.gl>
> # you could for example add the name of your species for each individual in the slot
> # other$ind.metrics
> # first how many individuals are there
> number_individuals <- nInd(gl)
> # setting half of individuals to be from species_1 and half for species_2
> gl$other$ind.metrics$species <- c(rep("species_1",number_individuals/2),rep("species_2",number_individuals/2))
> # The interactive plot uses individual names to fill the points and the population names
> # for the borders of the points. So, if you want one color for each species, you can
> # set the individual names and the populations names with the name of the species
> # as follows
> # setting species as individual names
> indNames(gl) <- gl$other$ind.metrics$species
> # setting species as population names
> pop(gl) <- gl$other$ind.metrics$species
> pca <- gl.pcoa(gl)
> pcoa_interactive2 <- gl.pcoa.plot(pca, gl, labels="interactive", xaxis=1, yaxis=2,verbose=5)
>
> On Tuesday, 29 June 2021 at 3:11:09 am UTC+10 dallasan...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Hello,
> >
> > Does anyone know if there is a way to color the points in an interactive PCoA by a specific group? For example, I'd like the points in my interactive PCoA to be colored by species. Here is my code if necessary:
> >
> > pcoa_interactive2 <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa2, gl2_complete, labels="interactive", xaxis=1, yaxis=2)
> > ggplotly()
> >
> > Thanks for your help!
> > Dallas
